title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1LC1LF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1LC1LF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks (10)^n separated by single 1s. In the right phase each sweep (head at the right end in state B) takes one 10 off the first block and appends a block (10)^3 1 at the right end; this rule is proved in Lean for every length. When the first block is used up, the left phase starts: the head bounces between the left end and a marker, the first block grows by 4 copies per two bounces while the block after the marker shrinks by 2, the marker moves through the list and rebuilds it (the left phase rules are also proved). Then a new right phase starts with a much longer first block (3,728 copies at 6.8·108 steps, used up at 1.234·109). No closed map yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 62,666 cells have been visited and 29,712 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).

claims.title: Right-phase sweep
claims.text: From the head at the right end in state B, one sweep turns (10)^(a+2) 1 [(10)^(b+2) 1] ((10)^3 1)^(n+1) into the same with one 10 less in the first block and one more block of three, in 4a+24n+53 steps (4a+4b+24n+73 with the middle block).

claims.title: Left-phase bounces
claims.text: From the head at the left end in state C: (01)^(x+2) 0 (01)^(y+3) 00110 goes to the marker and back in 4x+22 steps, the first block three copies longer and the marker now a 1; the next bounce (4x+26 steps) adds one more copy and restores the marker 0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A plain C simulator (longrun.c, on tools/c/tm.h) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the head has visited cells -586,772 to 108,199 and 329,462 cells hold a 1.

claims.title: The phases in the run
claims.text: In the direct run the right phases end (first block 0) at 8.0·10<sup>4</sup>, 1.96·10<sup>7</sup> and 1.234·10<sup>9</sup> steps; the left phases between them last until 8.3·10<sup>6</sup> and 6.5·10<sup>8</sup> steps, and the third lasts past 3·10<sup>9</sup>. From 1.234·10<sup>9</sup> to 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps the head reaches only the left end (47,163 times in state A, 23,587 in C), and the tail of 4655 blocks of three is left as it is.

claims.title: Growing phases, no sign of a halt
claims.text: Each right phase is longer than the last (its first block is built from the whole list in the left phase), and the list behind it is periodic in large stretches ([19,35]×15, [541,917]×11, [5,13]×13), the signature of a deterministic hierarchical counter rather than a random walk.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two phases are understood one sweep at a time, but the rebuilding of the list in the left phase has not been reduced to a map.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RF_1RD0RA_1LE0RC_1LC0LD_0RD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine alternates two phases: in one, each sweep moves one unit from the first block of the tape to a growing tail of small blocks; in the other, the head bounces at the left end and rebuilds a much longer first block from the whole list.

facts.text: One sweep of each phase, proved for every length.
Right phases ending at 8·10<sup>4</sup>, 2·10<sup>7</sup>, 1.2·10<sup>9</sup> steps, each round much longer.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: Countdown and rebuild
html: In the right phase the tape is (10)^a 1 (10)^b 1 … 1 (10)^3 1 (10)^3 1 …. Each sweep takes one 10 from the first block and appends a (10)^3 1 on the right; the blocks in between are left as they are:

When the first block is empty, the head stops reaching the right end and the left phase starts: the head bounces between the left end and a marker (a single 0 or 1), adding copies to the first block while taking them from the block behind the marker; the marker then moves on through the list, so the first block collects a share of every block. The next right phase starts with this long first block.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).
After 109 steps the tape spans 62,666 cells (44,552 left of the start, 2,149 right), with a density of 1s of 0.474.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RF_1RD0RA_1LE0RC_1LC0LD_0RD---: rename A→D, B→E, C→C, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1LB1LF_0LC---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state B

family: Two-phase list sweeper: a countdown block feeding a tail of (10)^3 blocks, then a left-growing bounce that rebuilds the list
summary: Blocks of (10)^n separated by single 1s: in one phase each sweep takes one 10 off the first block and appends a block of three at the right end; when the first block is empty, a long phase of bounces at the left end rebuilds the list with a marker that runs through it.
